newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. agency forecasts fall in rice trade in 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency forecasts fall in rice trade in 1997.

text.p: The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) forecast Monday that world trade in rice would fall this year on the back of an overall global weakening of demand.

"World trade in rice in 1997 is forecast to fall to 18.5 million tonnes, which would be 0.8 million tonnes lower than the volume traded in the previous year and 2.4 million tonnes below the record level achieved in 1995," FAO said in a report.
The Rome-based agency said Thailand, India and Vietnam had been hit most by a slackening in world demand for rice and exports were down substantially.

Thailand's exports fell 0.5 million tonnes in the first four months of 1997 compared to the same period last year. India was forecast to take an even sharper drop with exports only touching 2.5 million tonnes in 1997, down 26 percent on 1996.
FAO said Vietnam's rice exports were down to 450,000 tonnes in the first quarter of 1997, a fall of 25 percent on the same period in 1996.
Exports of rice out of Pakistan and China, however, were likely to remain strong in 1997, the report said.
The agency said international rice prices had been pushed down by the reduced trade and an abundant world supply following good paddy harvests in countries like Thailand and Vietnam.

"International rice prices fell sharply in April. The FAO price index for rice (1982/84=100) averaged 128.5, down from its March level and eight points below the level in April last year," the report said.
Indian rice prices rose despite a decrease in its exports, FAO said. This was due to a reduced domestic stock.
